display_name: Wind Gap Woodruff Vineyard Pinot Noir, Santa Cruz Mountains
raw_content:
{
  "hook": "Wind Gap’s Woodruff Vineyard Pinot sits at 1,800 ft on fractured shale and sandstone, catching morning fog through the Saratoga Gap—so you taste Pacific salt on red cranberry, not Central Valley jam. 2014 gave a tiny crop of 0.9 tons/acre; the wine clocks 12.8% alcohol yet carries five-second tannic grip, a combo that still puzzles Napa drinkers.",
  "wine_summary": "Wind Gap was the project Pax Mahle started in 2006 to prove that California could do low-alcohol, whole-cluster Pinot without saccharine oak. Woodruff is his coolest, highest site; in 2014 he used 40% stems and only 15% new François Frères 228-L barrels, so the wine reads like a Morey-St-Denis that took a ocean dip. Santa Cruz Mountains’ shale drains winter storms in hours, forcing roots into fractured seabed veins; the result is a Pinot with iron-rich snap that can stand next to $80 Sonoma Coast bottlings while priced like a weekday red.",
  "terroir_expression": "Decomposed shale and sandstone, shot through with iron oxide, give a ferrous, blood-orange edge to the red-cranberry fruit. At 1,800 ft the berries stay under 23° Brix even in warm years; diurnal swings of 25°F lock in malic acid so pH rarely tops 3.45. The Saratoga Gap funnels marine air, leaving a saline, nori-like note on the finish—think dried sage meets Pacific tidepool.",
  "vinification_summary": "40% whole clusters, native yeast, five-day cold soak to extract color without heat; no sulfur until first racking, preserving thiols that read as pink grapefruit zest. Aged 11 months in 15% new 228-L French oak, then six months in neutral stainless—Mahle calls it \"steel nap\" to tighten the mid-palate before bottling unfined/unfiltered.",
  "food_pairing": [
    "Nashville hot chicken sandwich—the high acid and stem tannin cut cayenne-spiked fry and refresh the palate.",
    "Dungeness crab cioppino with fennel pollen; seaweed note mirrors shellfish umami while tartness lifts tomato broth.",
    "Mushroom & nettle risotto: earthy porcini and green nettle bite echo the wine’s forest-floor savor without overwhelming its 12.8% frame.",
    "Tea-smoked duck breast, plum glaze—light body won’t overpower duck, whole-cluster spice handles five-spice rub.",
    "Aged goat goud crottin with lemon zest; shale-driven mineral snap plays off cheese’s chalky tang."
  ],
  "comparable_wines": [
    "Mount Eden Estate Pinot Noir 2012 — same mountain range, similar shale, older vines, more Bordeaux-like structure.",
    "Failla Sonoma Coast Pinot Noir 2014 — same winemaking credo, lower alcohol stem inclusion, slightly warmer fruit profile.",
    "Au Bon Climat ‘Bien Nacido’ Pinot 2013 — Santa Maria Valley sand, similar whole-cluster salinity, rounder mid-palate."
  ],
  "style_profile": "Light-bodied dry red with tart red-berry cut and stem-spice backbone",
  "cellar_recommendation": "Drink 2018-2028; keep at 55°F, 70% RH. The 2014’s low pH means it will stay bright, but stem tannins soften after year eight.",
  "value_assessment": "$38-45 retail. At that price it undercuts Mount Eden ($70) and Failla ($55) while delivering comparable mountain tension. You’re paying for site specificity, not brand gloss—worth it if you want Burgundy lift without the tariff.",
  "market_position": "You’ll spot it by-the-glass at Bay Area Cal-Italian spots (Che Fico, Trick Dog) and on boutique shelves in Berkeley or Portland. Buyers are somms who need a domestic Pinot under 13% to pour next to Jura—collectors chase the 2012, but casual drinkers like the drinkability.",
  "insider_take": "Skip the 2013 silver-medal vintage—it was rainy and shows green pepper. 2014 is the sleeper, but most shoppers overlook it because Santa Cruz Mountains isn’t on the glamour map; that’s your edge for cellar pricing before the region pops.",
  "aging_potential_years": 10,
  "drinking_window_min_years": 4,
  "drinking_window_max_years": 14,
  "sensory": {
    "acidity": 4,
    "tannin": 3,
    "body": 2,
    "sweetness": 1,
    "alcohol": 2,
    "color_intensity": "medium",
    "aroma_intensity": "pronounced",
    "finish_length": "long",
    "complexity": "complex",
    "quality_level": "very_good"
  }
}
